$comment: Entry schema for contributes.debuggers (process plugins that declare the shell capability, manifest apiVersion 2). Host validation lives in backend/plugin/contrib_debuggers.go (install) and debuggers_launch.go (prepare/confirm/start). type is unique across installed plugins. adapter.kind is one of {{lists.adapterKinds}}; for stdio and tcp the host starts every adapter process itself, after the user confirms the exact final command line (fingerprint: plugin id, version, file hashes and command line) in every approval mode, and stops it when the session ends or the plugin is disabled, uninstalled, reloaded or upgraded. A jdtls adapter starts no process: command must be a jdtls command this plugin declares in contributes.jdtlsBundles (no args or env); after the same confirmation (fingerprint: plugin id, version, jar hashes, command) the host runs it in the built-in Java language service, which must have the plugin's confirmed jars loaded, and connects to the loopback port it returns. adapter.command follows the languageServers rules (bare program name or ${pluginRoot}/<relative>) and may also be ${resolved.<name>}, which must resolve to an existing regular executable. For tcp adapters the host picks a loopback port, substitutes ${port} in args and connects within {{limits.tcpConnectTimeoutMs}} ms. env names on the contract denylist are rejected at install and at launch. resolveAction, entryPointsAction, checkAction and settingsAction name this plugin's own read-risk, non-aiCallable actions; resolve must have no side effects, runs at most {{limits.resolveTimeoutMs}} ms and returns at most {{limits.resolveResultMaxBytes}} bytes; entry points time out after {{limits.entryPointsTimeoutMs}} ms and are capped at {{limits.entryPointsMax}}; check times out after {{limits.checkTimeoutMs}} ms; settings (exceptionTypes) after {{limits.settingsTimeoutMs}} ms. A start sends at most {{limits.functionBreakpointsMax}} function and {{limits.dataBreakpointsMax}} data breakpoints, only to adapters that declare supportsFunctionBreakpoints / supportsDataBreakpoints. DAP frames are capped at {{limits.messageMaxBytes}} bytes, stderr at {{limits.stderrMaxBytes}} bytes, and a plugin runs at most {{limits.sessionsPerPlugin}} sessions. AI tools cannot list or start debug sessions.
description: Debuggers: Debug Adapter Protocol adapters for editor languages, started by the host after the user confirms the exact command line.

type.description: Debugger type id that run configurations refer to; unique across installed plugins.

languages.description: Editor language ids (built-in or contributes.languages ids).

command.description: A bare program name, ${pluginRoot}/<relative path> or ${resolved.<name>}. No shell runs in between: $VAR stays literal. For kind jdtls: a jdtls command declared in this plugin's contributes.jdtlsBundles.

args.description: At most {{limits.argsTotalBytes}} bytes in total. May use ${pluginRoot}, ${projectRoot} and ${resolved.<name>}; a tcp adapter must pass ${port} (stdio adapters may not use it); a jdtls adapter takes no args or env.

resolveAction.description: Id of one of this plugin's contributes.actions with risk 'read' and aiCallable false; it must have no side effects.

entryPointsAction.description: Id of one of this plugin's contributes.actions with risk 'read' and aiCallable false.

checkAction.description: Id of one of this plugin's contributes.actions with risk 'read' and aiCallable false.

settingsAction.description: Id of one of this plugin's contributes.actions with risk 'read', aiCallable false and maxPayloadBytes of at least {{limits.settingsPayloadMinBytes}}. The host calls it with {type, project: {root}, exceptionTypes} before a session of this type is prepared and when the user changes the list while a session of the project runs; it must return {} within {{limits.settingsTimeoutMs}} ms. exceptionTypes is always sent, as [] when the list is empty, so the plugin clears its previous filter.

exceptionTypes.description: Declares the host's 'pause only on these exception types' list for this debugger type (saved per project); requires settingsAction. Texts are single-line plain text. The host keeps at most {{limits.exceptionTypesMax}} distinct items of at most {{limits.exceptionTypeMaxRunes}} characters, each a dotted identifier matching ^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*(\.[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)*$ after trimming.

functionBreakpoints.description: Declares the host's method breakpoint input for this debugger type and its texts (placeholder: the name format the adapter accepts). Texts are single-line plain text. The breakpoints dialog shows the method breakpoint section only for debuggers that declare it; the saved names are sent (setFunctionBreakpoints, at most {{limits.functionBreakpointsMax}}) only to sessions whose adapter declares supportsFunctionBreakpoints. The host never parses the names.

event.description: The adapter's custom DAP event that reports recompiled code.

request.description: The adapter's custom DAP request that applies the recompiled code.

modeSetting.description: The key of this plugin's own contributes.configuration property that holds the hot code replace mode: a global, non-secret string setting with enum exactly auto, manual, never. The host reads it when the adapter reports a build; without it the mode is auto.

hotCodeReplace.description: Declares the adapter's hot code replace extension: a custom DAP event and request name, and optionally the setting that holds the mode. Neither name may be a DAP standard request or event name (compared case-insensitively). The host shows its apply-code-changes controls only for debuggers that declare it. The adapter must follow the host's hot code replace event protocol v1 as documented in plugin-development.md (debuggers, hotCodeReplace): the event body is {changeType, message?}, where changeType BUILD_COMPLETE means the build can be applied, WARNING and ERROR show message as it is, and other values are progress the host ignores; the request takes no arguments and answers {changedClasses?: string[], errorMessage?: string} (the replaced type names, or why nothing or not everything was replaced).

configurationSchema.description: Form schema for launch and attach configurations; at most {{limits.schemaMaxBytes}} bytes.

configurationSnippets.description: Templates for new run configurations; at most {{limits.snippetMaxBytes}} bytes each.

argsTemplate.description: Server-side arguments shown to the user to copy; never run by the host.
